# S47 — Release signing from environment or keystore.properties, unsigned fallback

**Findings:** app/build.gradle:25-30 (no signingConfig); .gitignore (keystores ignored, keystore.properties is not) · **Size:** S · **Tree:** release

**Not in this slice:** the GitHub release workflow (S21), R8 (S19), and creating the real release keystore (the owner does that and never commits it).

## Why

- `assembleRelease` currently produces an unsigned APK with no way to sign it.
- GitHub releases need a signed APK. F-Droid builds from source and signs with its own key, so the build must also work with no keystore at all.

## Files

- `app/build.gradle`
- `.gitignore`
- `DEVELOPERS.md` ("Signing for release" section)

## Failing tests

- None. Checked by building both ways.

## Implement

1. Read signing values from `keystore.properties` in the repo root (keys `storeFile`, `storePassword`, `keyAlias`, `keyPassword`), falling back to the environment variables `CONSECUTOR_KEYSTORE` (a path), `CONSECUTOR_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `CONSECUTOR_KEY_ALIAS` and `CONSECUTOR_KEY_PASSWORD`.
2. Define `signingConfigs.release` only when all four values are present. Set `buildTypes.release.signingConfig = signingConfigs.release` only in that case. With any value missing the release build stays unsigned and still succeeds.
3. Add `keystore.properties` to `.gitignore`.
4. Update `DEVELOPERS.md` with the file format, the variable names and the "unsigned if absent" behaviour. Do not put real values in the repo, the docs or any log. Never print a password.

## Check

- With nothing configured, `./gradlew assembleRelease` succeeds and produces `app-release-unsigned.apk`.
- Generate a throwaway keystore in the scratchpad with `keytool -genkeypair` and point the environment variables at it. `assembleRelease` then produces a signed APK, and `apksigner verify --print-certs` (from the Android build-tools) passes. Delete the throwaway keystore afterwards.
- `git status` shows no keystore or properties file.
